# Studienstiftung Summary
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes (German National Academic Foundation) was founded in Dresden in 1925, dissolved in 1934, and re-established in 1948 in Cologne. It is Germany's largest and most prestigious scholarship organization, supporting exceptionally talented university and doctoral students based on principles of excellence, initiative, and responsibility. Admission is highly selective, relying on nominations from schools, professors, examination boards, competition winners, cooperation partners, assessment tests, alumni, and institutional nominations for artists and musicians. The foundation is open to students studying full-time at universities in Germany, EU, or Switzerland, without requirements for German or EU citizenship or age. Scholarships are generally awarded until the end of standard study periods, with extensions possible based on performance and personal circumstances.
Studienstiftung scholarships consist of financial support (monthly allowance, insurance subsidies, means-tested scholarships up to €855/month, and special funding for students/PhD students with children) and substantial academic support via summer schools, research groups, mentoring, and event organization. Doctoral scholars receive higher stipends and research allowances. Additional programs are available, such as international partnerships and special internal and external scholarships (e.g., Max Weber program). In 2023, there were 14,888 scholars (including 1,262 doctoral candidates), about 0.48% of German students, with women comprising 55.4%. Notable alumni include Nobel laureates, influential academics, business leaders, politicians, artists, and journalists.
